starting-off.text: If the player is missing one or more requirements:

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Sorry to have bothered you; I'm looking for a more experienced adventurer.

starting-off.text: If the player has all of the requirements to start the quest:

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: I'm looking for a bold and true adventurer to help me with a...a...a little problem?

steps.player: Well you've found one... Say, you don't look much like a pirate.
In fact, you look a little ill.
A little more than ill, in fact...

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Shhh!

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: That's all part of the problem...and we can't talk here.

steps.player: This is starting to sound a little bit dodgy, and I do appreciate I'm in a hive of scum and villainy as I say this.
Is there any part of your problem you can tell me?

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Well, all I can say is that I am from a small, cloistered order of monks from a tiny island nearby, and that we have a problem with undead pirates...

steps.prompt: Start The Great Brain Robbery quest?

steps.player: Undead pirates? Let me at em!

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Oh, you'll help? Wonderful!

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Now, I'll just transport us to the island...
The player performs the quiver emote.

steps.player: No hitting! No hitting!

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Are you all right, my child?

steps.player: Sorry, sorry.
I just get this thumping pain in the back of my head whenever I think about travelling to an island full of undead pirates.
I have no idea why.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Hmm, that is odd. Have you considered seeing a doctor?

steps.player: No, but I might well do soon if it keeps up.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Anyway, I'll just use the teleport spell I created. Let's go!
The player is teleported to Harmony Island.

steps.player: Zombies! Back away from those monks now!

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: Wait! Wait! We ARE monks!

steps.player: What? Seriously? Zombie monks?

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Honestly, they are with us, and they aren't zombies.

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Sort of, at any rate.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: It's true. We need your help...will you at least listen to us?

steps.player: Okay, but the first one of you that lunges for my brain will be strung up and beaten until they are dead...or very, very sorry.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Oh, but of course. I understand that this is very confusing.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: We are a cloistered order of Saradominist monks. We use this island's relative isolation to translate and illuminate books. We even have a treaty with the pirates; they leave us alone and we provide the occasional

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: blessing they might need.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: This morning, however, we were awakened by the sound of a ship running aground and, as we readied ourselves to venture out to look for survivors, zombie pirates poured into the monastery.

steps.player: Were they particularly drunken-looking?

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Not that we could tell. They seemed to be being given orders by a twisted little zombie called Mi-Gor and his cadre of sorebones.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Some of us, like myself, were dragged away.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: I remember a terrible pain, and then woke up in this body with Mi-Gor nearby, gloating about having 'enhanced' a zombie with a non-rotting brain.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: I laid low, pretending to still be unconscious and, after a while, made my move, freeing the others that had been 'enhanced'.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: We fought our way to the granary and have barred the doors. We stored our now brainless bodies downstairs in case we can be put back to normal.

steps.player: And what have they done as a result?

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: It looked like they were going to storm the doors, but then Mi-Gor called them off.

steps.player: Called them off? Any idea why?

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: No, none whatsoever.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Now that you know our plight, will you help us?

steps.player: Of course!

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Saradomin be praised!

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: There is a secret tunnel into the monastery under the statue in the garden. If you get inside, you can find out what they are planning and we can counter it.

steps.player: Well good luck with that.

starting-off-talking-to-brother-tranquil.speaker: Brother Tranquility
starting-off-talking-to-brother-tranquil.text: Have you thought any more about helping our order?

starting-off-talking-to-brother-tranquil.player: Er, I might have done. What was the problem again?

starting-off-talking-to-brother-tranquil.speaker: Brother Tranquility
starting-off-talking-to-brother-tranquil.text: Our island has been overrun by undead pirates.

starting-off-talking-to-brother-tranquil.prompt: Start The Great Brain Robbery quest?

starting-off-talking-to-brother-tranquil.speaker: Brother Tranquility
starting-off-talking-to-brother-tranquil.text: So, have you found anything out about the pirates' plans?

options.text: Could you take me back to port?

steps.text: The player is teleported back to Mos Le'Harmless.

steps.player: Nothing yet... What would you recommend doing again?

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Well, the secret passage into the monastery is located in the gardens.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: If you pull the statue there out of the way you'll be able to get into the tunnels, and from there into the monastery.

steps.player: Thanks!

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: What if I start craving brains?

steps.player: Just eat a cauliflower or something!

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: I don't even know what one of those is!

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: This is so awful...

steps.player: Hang in there, brother, [player name] is on the case.

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: Something fell off! Something fell off!

steps.player: I don't wanna know!

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: I wish I was back in my own body.

steps.player: I'm working on it, okay? Give me a minute.

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: I can feel my brain thumping about in here when I shake my head.

steps.player: Then try to stay still!

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: I don't want to be stuck this way!

steps.player: You won't be, trust me!

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: This body feels itchy...

steps.player: Likely that's all in the mind...
Sorry! Sorry!

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: I suppose I should view this as a test of faith...

steps.player: That's the spirit!

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Except the holy texts are light on plagues of zombie pirates.

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Zombies! What ever will we do?

steps.player: Keep calm. I'm a professional. I'll take care of it.

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: I knew I should have been a bricklayer...

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: I don't want to lose my brain!

steps.player: You won't, trust me!

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: I was almost all the way through translating that book too...

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: What if they get in while I'm asleep? Oh no!

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: So, have you dealt with this sort of problem before?

steps.player: Sure, although the zombies were drunker, the hostages were less holy and the island was known for exporting swill, not piety.

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Oh, well that's okay then.

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Glabburbleglubble...

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Blubblelubblebubblelubble...

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Plib!

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Blublublubluh...

starting-off-talking-to-the-monks-inside.player: Wow, without a brain, these monks seem a lot less holy all of a sudden...

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: I don't want to be stuck this way!

steps.player: You won't be, trust me!

steps.speaker: Zombie monk
steps.text: Something fell off! Something fell off!

steps.player: I don't wanna know!

starting-off-exploring-the-island-before.text: You do not need some fuse from there right now.
You do not need one of those at the moment.
You cannot go in there now; it would probably give away the monks' plan.
The player pulls the statue to the west.
You pull the statue, revealing the hole underneath...
If the player climbs down the hole whilst wearing a diving apparatus and a fishing bowl:

steps.text: You climb down into a dank, cramped cavern.
It seems this area is flooded. Good job you have your diving equipment!

starting-off-exploring-the-island-before.text: If the player climbs down the hole without wearing the diving apparatus and a fishing bowl:
If the player attempts to ascend down the stairs without wearing the diving gear:

steps.text: You cannot go diving without your diving helmet and diving apparatus!

starting-off-exploring-the-island-before.text: If the player ascends down the stairs whilst wearing their diving gear:

steps.text: The player enters water-flooded stairs.

starting-off-exploring-the-island-before.text: If the player attempts to repair the hammer without the required materials:

steps.text: You need a hammer, 10 nails and 4 normal planks to repair the broken stairs.

starting-off-exploring-the-island-before.text: If the player attempts to climb the broken stairs:

steps.text: You cannot climb these until you have repaired them.

starting-off-exploring-the-island-before.text: If the player successfully repairs the steps:

steps.text: You repair the steps.

starting-off-exploring-the-island-before.text: If the player attempts to remove either the apparatus or fishbowl helmet on the other side of the tunnel:

steps.text: If you remove that, how will you get back to the other side of the flooded tunnel?

starting-off-sneaking-past-the-tunnel-in.text: If the player looks into the peephole to the temple:

steps.text: You look through the peephole in the wall into the main body of the monastery and overhear the following conversation:

steps.speaker: Mi-Gor
steps.text: Wheeze* I have received a summons to attend to the Captain and so will be 'down below' for a while.
That voice can't help but make you shudder. It sounds like the speaker is trying to talk through a throat filled with mud.

steps.speaker: Mi-Gor
steps.text: Wheeze* How is the gas production progressing?

steps.speaker: Sorebones
steps.text: Arr, it be progressin' well...

steps.speaker: Mi-Gor
steps.text: Wheeze* What is it? I can smell your lie, whelp.

steps.speaker: Sorebones
steps.text: No, no! 'Tis just that we need more ingredients fer enough te blanket the island!

steps.speaker: Sorebones
steps.text: If ye'd just let us storm the granary we'd be able te take them monks out real easy like.

steps.speaker: Sorebones
steps.text: Why, that thing of yers could hammer the wall down...

steps.speaker: Mi-Gor
steps.text: Wheeze!* Silence! I will not be questioned by underlings!

steps.speaker: Mi-Gor
steps.text: Wheeze* If you or the others do not consider yourselves capable of carrying out Rabid Jack's orders, then perhaps you need to spend some time in 'The Box'!

steps.player: Rabid Jack! That name again...

steps.text: You peer back through the peep-hole.

steps.speaker: Sorebones
steps.text: Please, no! Not 'The Box'!

steps.speaker: Sorebones
steps.text: The sleeping gas will be ready as planned, Surgeon General. Those monks will be takin' a nap for a week when they get a whiff of it, and the experiments will not stand a chance.

steps.speaker: Mi-Gor
steps.text: Wheeze* Excellent...the gas will leave the brain intact for the next stage.

steps.speaker: Mi-Gor
steps.text: Wheeze* This time there will be no rebellion amongst the subjects.

steps.speaker: Mi-Gor
steps.text: Wheeze* Rabid Jack will have his crew of enhanced zombies and I will have as many test subjects as I can vivisect!

steps.speaker: Mi-Gor
steps.text: Wheeze* Hekhekhekhek!

steps.player: Sleeping gas! I have to tell the monks about this right now! I only hope I have time...

starting-off-sneaking-past-the-tunnel-in.text: If the player attempts to peer-through the peephole again:

steps.text: You do not think there will be anything interesting to see through that.

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.text: So, have you found anything out about the pirates' plans?

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.player: The pirates are planning on using some sort of sleeping gas to knock you all out!
When everyone is unconscious, they are going to come in and take you away for brain-swaps!

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.text: We have to prepare our defence against this threat. I recall something that might well help...

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.player: Is it some sort of potion to counteract the poison?

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.text: No, no. You see, the gas will work on us faster than a normal poison, and a potion would take too long to diffuse through the stomach.

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.text: No, what I'm thinking of is a prayer written centuries ago by one of the abbots at the Edgeville Monastery.

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.player: Hmm, how come I've never heard of this prayer?

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.text: Well, the abbot was slain by a group of raiders. Apparently his faith was little protection against their repeated sword blows.

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.text: Anyway, the book of prayers he wrote was stored in the Edgeville Monastery, so you will need to go there and retrieve it. And quickly!

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility.text: Here, I'll take you straight back to Mos Le'Harmless.
Brother Tranquility teleports the player back to Harmony Island.

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility-ta.text: If the player does not have the book:

steps.player: No, I don't.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Oh, well hurry to the Edgeville Monastery and get it. We haven't got a moment to lose!

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility-ta.text: If the player has the book in their bank:

steps.player: Yes, in my bank.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: What use is it there? Go get it and hurry back. We haven't got a moment to lose!

reporting-back-to-brother-tranquility-ta.text: If the player has the book in their inventory:

steps.player: Yes, I have your book here.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: When you took the book from the shelf, did you say the words?

steps.player: Words? What words?

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: The words! The words of power that would prevent...

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Wait a moment, I forgot to tell you them, didn't I?

steps.player: Yes! There were no words! What were they supposed to prevent?

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Oh dear...in all the excitement I completely forgot about them...

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: I do hope that we can fix things before the locusts arrive...

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Silly me, all this excitement - and likely that crude brain-operation - made me totally forget. I'm sure that it'll all work out somehow.

steps.player: LOCUSTS?

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Oh, don't worry, it'll only be a little swarm.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Now, back to business.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: So have you read the book?
If the player has not read the book:

steps.player: No, not yet.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquillity
steps.text: Well, you should give it a try now, just in case there is anything else you need.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquillity
steps.text: No point in going all the way to Harmony and then back because you need something else.
If the player already read the book:

steps.player: Yes, I have read the prayer and I know how to perform it.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Great! Do you have everything you'll need?
If the player does not have the holy symbol:

steps.player: No, I need to go and get a holy symbol.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquility
steps.text: Well hurry! Who knows what depredations are going on back on Harmony!
If the player has the holy symbol:

steps.player: Yes, I have the book and the holy symbol I need.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquillity
steps.text: Excellent! Back to Harmony!
The player is teleported to Harmony Island.

steps.speaker: Brother Tranquillity
steps.text: Quickly, the pirates have released the gas! Use the prayer. The other brothers will help make it powerful enough to cover the whole of the granary.

finding-the-book-of-prayers.text: If the player searches the bookcase where the book of prayers isn't found:

steps.text: You search the books...
You find nothing to interest you.

finding-the-book-of-prayers.text: If the player searches the bookcase where the book of prayers is found:

steps.text: You have found the book of prayers!

finding-the-book-of-prayers.text: If the player searches the bookcase again after retrieving the book of prayers:

steps.text: You find a gap in the shelves where the book of prayers would go.
As it is in your backpack you know that it is unlikely to be hidden on the shelf again.

finding-the-book-of-prayers-interacting-.text: If the player clicks on the "Recite-prayer" option on the book:

steps.text: You will need to read the book first.

finding-the-book-of-prayers-interacting-.text: If the player reads the book:

steps.text: The book details a prayer to Saradomin for aid against poisons. The caster must wear a blessed symbol of Saradomin or the prayer will fail.

finding-the-book-of-prayers-interacting-.text: If the player clicks on the "Recite-prayer" option on the book after reading (without wearing the blessed symbol):

steps.text: You need to be wearing a blessed symbol of Saradomin for the prayer to work.

finding-the-book-of-prayers-interacting-.text: If the player clicks on the "Recite-prayer" option on the book after reading (whilst reading the blessed symbol:

steps.text: If the player is not currently poisoned:
You recite the prayer even though you are unpoisoned.
If player is currently poisoned:
If the player does not have Prayer points:
You recite the prayer even though you have no prayer points.
If the player has a certain amount of Prayer points:
You recite the prayer...
...and the power of Saradomin cures you of poison.
The player's poison is cured.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: Quickly, the pirates have released the gas! Use the prayer, the other brothers will help make it powerful enough to cover the whole of the granary.
If the player recites the prayer with the book but is not wearing the holy symbol:

steps.text: You need to be wearing a blessed symbol of Saradomin for the prayer to work.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: If the player recites the prayer whilst wearing the holy symbol:

steps.text: You recite the prayer and the monks chant along with you.
The smell of gas vanishes; the granary has been warded against the knockout effect.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: The player collapses, and is sent back to the granary.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: Are you alright? We dragged you back inside as quickly as we could.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.player: Woah...that gas is pretty potent... I'll need to wear my diving gear outside so that I don't get knocked out again.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: So long as you are unharmed, that is the main thing.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: Well done! The power of Saradomin will keep the poison from affecting anyone within these walls.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.player: So what now? Want me to go and kill the zombies?

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: Well, fun as that would be, I was wondering if you could help us get our brains back into the right bodies.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.player: You know, that was what I was going to suggest next.
So what do you want me to do, scrub up and grab a pair of pliers or something?

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: While I trust your skills in all other areas, I can state without fear of contradiction when I say that you are not a brain surgeon.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: No, what we want you to do is bring Doctor Fenkenstrain to us to do the operation.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.player: That evil, demented, eye-rollingly insane butcher? What could you want with him and his twisted...

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: In addition to wanting him to come here and help us, we also would like to let the poor soul atone for his sins and for his attempts to meddle in domains into which man was never meant to pry.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: Basically, I think when you tell him we have a werewolf- free place for him here on the island, I'm sure he'll agree to come.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.player: Well, I cant say I agree with this...but I do appreciate that he's likely the only person that knows his way around the inside of someone's skull.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: You have my word that he will not be able to continue his depraved experiments here on this island and will instead be moulded into a useful and faithful follower of Saradomin.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: Tell him that he is welcome here in exchange for his help.

steps.text: The player is teleported back to Mos Le'Harmless.

steps.player: Not at the moment, thanks.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.player: I haven't been to see him yet.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: Well, when you do, try your best to persuade him to help.

at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.speaker: Brother Tranquility
at-harmony-island-cursed-with-poison-gas.text: Want me to take you back to Mos Le'Harmless?

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: Are they here yet? I can hear them...howling!

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.player: For all the things you've done, I'd like to pour barbecue sauce on your head and pitch you out that window.
Instead, I've come to offer you a way out of this castle.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: Anything, anything. I will do anything to escape the wolves!

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.player: Would you perform multiple brain surgeries on a number of zombie monks?
I think you heard me. A number of monks on an island off the coast of Mos Le'Harmless have had their brains placed in zombie pirate bodies, and vice versa, and they want you to switch them back.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: I see...and how long have you been hearing these 'monks' talking to you?

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.player: Hands up, everyone who is being hunted by packs of ravenous killer werewolves!
Oh, why, that would be you, doctor.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: I mean, you have to admit that this is a little...unlikely a scenario.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.player: Oh yes, I'm sure that a man that stitches corpses together for a living would be a good judge of rationality.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: Did you come here to ask me something or just to insult me?

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: And my medical practice was my living. The corpses thing was just a hobby.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.player: Yes, I came here to tell you that a group of monks need your services, and that they are willing to shelter you from the werewolves if you will use your medical skills to help them.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: Hmm, sounds like an offer I'd have to be really mad to refuse...

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: I accept, but you'll have to get me past those werewolves.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.player: Well, you've lived here long enough. Is there some way I can smuggle you past?

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: Hmm, their sense of smell is quite acute, so no disguise would work. And I have a slight...reaction...to teleporting.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: Wait... Rufus might be able to help.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.text: Well, he occasionally delivers meat to clients if they are too far away to come and get it themselves. If I were inside a crate of meat then he'd be unable to smell me and you'd be able to get me past.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain.player: Okay, that seems sensible. I'll be right back.

steps.text: If the player is not wearing the Ring of Charos:
Since you are not wearing the Ring of Charos, you will be unable to convince Rufus you are a werewolf, and so he is unlikely to deliver meat for you.
If the player is wearing the Ring of Charos:

steps.player: Hey, Rufus, I heard that you do deliveries of meat. Could you send me a crate of supplies to Mos Le'Harmless?

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Well, it's a bit of a way to go, but for you, I'd wrrrite up a shipping orderrr.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: What do you want to send?

steps.player: Er, some meat?

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Well, I didn't think you wanted to send shoes, frrriend; this is a meat shop. What I mean is, what KIND of meat do you want to send?

steps.player: Oh, don't worry about it, I'll be providing the meat myself. It's a treat for some werewolves down there, you see.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Hmm, I hadn't hearrrd about any packs running with the pirrrates...still, I trust you.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Look, I apprrreciate you'rrre wanting to catch the meat yourrrself, I mean that's the sort of wolf I am too, but therrre is one thing.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: I'll gladly give you a crate for the meat, but I'll have to inspect it beforrre you send it over. I don't want my name associated with anything less than 100% frrresh, you understand.

steps.player: Oh sure, that's entirely reasonable.

steps.text: If the player has no inventory space:

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Grrreat! I have the parrrts for the crrrate forrr you when you have the space to carrrry them.
If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Grrreat! Here's the parrrts of the crrrate. Sorrrry, but I seem to be out of nails.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: So, can I get a hint as to what you arrre sending?

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Rrrabbits? Ducks? Sheep?

steps.player: Oh, I'm sure that I'll be able to find some good meat from somewhere.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Wait, you are sending it live, rrright?

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: I mean it is going to take a while to get therrre, so I'm not going to ship it unless it's at least a little alive.

steps.player: What?
Err, I mean, what do you mean only a little alive? Of course a good werewolf like me will be sending the food live.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Ha, ha, ha! Of courrrse, of course!

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: So, what can I expect to see when I inspect this shipment of yourrrs?

steps.player: Errr, you know, something...special...

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: It's cats isn't it?

steps.player: Cats?

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Oh, don't worrrry, you sly dog, I'll not tell anyone.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Tell you what, I'll get the shipping order for a crrrate of cats wrrritten up rrright now. You just provide the meat.

steps.player: But...

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: No buts, frrriend, you get going. I know how trrricky those things are to grab!
If the player has no inventory space for the whistle:

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: You're carrying too much for me to give this to you now, but I have a whistle you can blow to call me when you have the crrrate filled.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Come talk to me when you have some frrree space forrr it.
If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Here, when you need me to inspect the meat, give this a blow and we'll get those tasty kitties of yours shipped off lickety split!
A cutscene starts with the player pondering on where to get the cats...

steps.player: Well, at least I got him to agree to ship the crate for me.
I suppose in the meantime I'll set the crate up in Fenkenstrain's tower where he can get to it.
All I have to do now is get a load of cats from somewhere...

steps.text: Elfinlocks walks by Rufus' store with their mechanical cat.

steps.speaker: Elfinlocks
steps.text: Keep up, cat!

steps.speaker: Clockwork cat
steps.text: Click, whirr!

steps.player: Of course! I'll make some fake cats from wood and fur!
With a little help from the Ring of Charos, he'll never know the difference.
It's just crazy enough to work...

steps.text: You can now craft wooden cats in the workshop of a player-owned house! Note: this need not be your own house.
If the player lost the wolf whistle:

steps.player: Rufus, can I have a wolf whistle?

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Well, I have plenty, but you seem to have no space for it. Come back when you do.
If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Surrre! Here you go.
another wolf whistle
If the player lost the crate parts:

steps.player: Rufus, can I have some crate parts?

steps.text: If the player does not have inventory space:

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Well surrre, as soon as you have some frrree space for them.
If the player has inventory space:

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Yes, herrre are some new ones.
more crate parts

talking-to-rufus-talking-to-dr-fenkenstr.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-rufus-talking-to-dr-fenkenstr.text: So how is the plan progressing?
If the player has not talked to Rufus:

steps.player: I still need to talk to Rufus.

talking-to-rufus-talking-to-dr-fenkenstr.text: If the player talked to Rufus:

steps.player: I have got Rufus to agree to let me ship some meat, but I have to build the crate and fill it with fake cats first.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Cats? He thought you were shipping cats?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Well, I don't know...if you were a werewolf, I can see you would strike him as THAT sort of person.

steps.player: What? Wait? What sort of person?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Oh, it's nothing to worry about.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Hahahahahahahahahaha! Cats...it all makes sense...

steps.player: I get the feeling I'm being maligned...

building-the-crate.text: If the player does not have a hammer, nails, and parts:

steps.text: You need a hammer, 20 nails and all 6 parts of the crate that Rufus gave you before you can do that.

building-the-crate.text: If the player has all of the needed parts:

steps.text: The player begins building the crate and may bend a few nails.
If the player runs out of nails whilst building the crate:
You don't have enough nails left.

building-the-crate.text: If the player has finished building the crate:

steps.text: You build the crate.

building-the-crate-talking-to-dr-fenkens.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
building-the-crate-talking-to-dr-fenkens.text: Well, that's a nice crate, but unless you want me to sit under a layer of (heh heh) cats, I think it'll need a false bottom.

building-the-crate-talking-to-dr-fenkens.player: Fine. And if you keep up these cat remarks I'm going to make sure the crate is shipped upside down, and not give you any padding.

building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.text: If the player does not have a hammer, nails, and parts:

steps.text: You need a hammer, 8 nails and 4 normal planks to construct the false bottom of the crate.

building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.text: If the player has all the required materials:

steps.text: The player starts building the false bottom of the crate.
If the player has ran out of nails whilst building the false bottom:
You don't have enough nails left.
If the player has built the false bottom:
You build a false bottom into the crate.

building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.text: Well, it'll be a tight fit, but I'm sure I'll be able to squeeze in.

building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.text: Now all you have to do is go and get all your little kitty friends!

building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.player: Be quiet or I'm going to post this thing direct to Canifis!
What is with this whole cat thing anyway?

building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.text: Nothing you need to worry about.

building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.text: Mwuhahahahahahaha! Oh, it's so apt, I can't stop laughing!

building-the-crate-building-the-false-bo.player: That does it, I'm leaving some nails in the bottom of the crate for him to sit on...

building-the-crate-storing-the-mechanica.text: If the player stores anything other than a cat or a noted clockwork cat:

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

building-the-crate-storing-the-mechanica.text: If the player stores fewer than 10 mechanical cats:

steps.text: You add a few fake cats to the crate, but not enough to cover the false bottom.
You think [#] more will cover it.

building-the-crate-storing-the-mechanica.text: If the player fills the crate with 10 cats:

steps.text: You fill the crate with fake cats.

building-the-crate-storing-the-mechanica.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
building-the-crate-storing-the-mechanica.text: Well, you certainly seem to know what you are doing when it comes to rounding up cats. You must get a lot of practice!

building-the-crate-storing-the-mechanica.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
building-the-crate-storing-the-mechanica.text: Well, regardless, everything seems to be ready for you to call Rufus.

building-the-crate-storing-the-mechanica.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
building-the-crate-storing-the-mechanica.text: Blow your whistle and I'll get in the crate while we wait.

smuggling-dr-fenkenstrain-out-of-the-cas.text: If the player attempts to summon Rufus whilst wearing a fishbowl helmet:

steps.text: You should take your diving helmet off before you try to blow the whistle.

smuggling-dr-fenkenstrain-out-of-the-cas.text: If the player attempts to summon Rufus without equipping the Ring of Charos:

steps.text: You will have a hard time convincing Rufus that these cats are real if you are not wearing the Ring of Charos.

smuggling-dr-fenkenstrain-out-of-the-cas.text: If the player successfully summons Rufus:

steps.player: Okay, Doctor, time to get in the crate.
Let's hope this works...

steps.text: A cutscene begins.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Well, frrriend, I take it you have-
Rufus pauses and looks around in shock.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: What are you doing herrre of all places? Don't you smell that weedy human, Fenkenstrrrain?

steps.player: Well yeah, but this was the only place I could think of to store the cats.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Well, I know I wouldn't want anyone to find out I had a habit like yourrrs, but still...

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: I take it this is the crrrate?

steps.player: That it is!

steps.text: Rufus looks at the crate and performs the Think emote.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: You know, they look verrry still...

steps.player: They must be pining.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Pining?

steps.player: Yes. Pining.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Seems rrreasonable. Is that why they arrren't making any noise?

steps.speaker: Box of cats
steps.text: Err...meow?

steps.player: See, they made a noise.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: You know, I think therrre might be...

steps.player: Nothing wrong whatsoever.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: ...nothing wrrrrong whatsoever!

steps.speaker: Box of cats
steps.text: Meow?

steps.player: I think the meowing point has been more than made.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Herrre is the shipping orderrr. Just paste it to send that crrrate on its way!
a shipping order and Rufus takes his whistle back

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: Although I'd prefer it if you took yourrr cat habit elsewherrre in futurrre. You understand, rrright?

steps.player: I don't, but I'll promise you this is the last time I do this.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: That's good. You should rrreally kick the habit beforrre it gets too late.

steps.speaker: Rufus
steps.text: See you laterrr, frrriend!

steps.player: Yeah, Rufus, see you around!

steps.speaker: Fenkenstrain in a box
steps.text: Has he gone?

steps.player: Yes, he's gone.

steps.speaker: Fenkenstrain in a box
steps.text: I liked the part where he asked you to keep your cat habit to yourself.

steps.player: Bear in mind I can still post you to Canifis if I choose!
Gah...let's get this over with...

steps.text: The cutscene ends.

smuggling-dr-fenkenstrain-out-of-the-cas.text: If the player uses the shipping order on the crate:

steps.text: You paste the shipping order to the crate and it vanishes!

steps.player: It teleported...but didn't he say he was allergic...
Oh dear, I do hope the doctor's reaction is not too violent.

talking-to-brother-tranquility-at-mos-le.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility-at-mos-le.text: The doctor was delivered safely, although it seems like a bunch of pirates have stolen your cats.

talking-to-brother-tranquility-at-mos-le.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility-at-mos-le.text: Would you like me to take you to Harmony?

steps.text: Brother Tranquility teleports the player to Harmony Island.

talking-to-brother-tranquility-at-harmon.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility-at-harmon.text: Well, the doctor is downstairs, waiting for you. I think he said he needed some things before he could begin.

talking-to-brother-tranquility-at-harmon.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility-at-harmon.text: Want me to take you back to Mos Le'Harmless?

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.player: I was entirely unaware of at least one of those teleports.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.text: I told you I reacted badly to teleportation!

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.text: Well, on the plus side, there was plenty of water to clean my clothing with afterwards...

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.text: Aside from that, I seem to have arrived in one piece. I apologise for not believing you earlier. Brother Tranquility has told me the full story and I am prepared to help.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.text: However, I am going to need a few things.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.text: I will need a cranial clamp, a pair of brain tongs, three bell jars and at least thirty skull staples.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.player: Where do you suggest I get these things, 'Unusual Implements R Us'?

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.text: Well, the zombies holed up in the main monastery must have at least one set of those items; otherwise, how did they perform the operation in the first place?

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.player: A fair point. I'll pop back through that secret passage and ambush them.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.text: That won't work. Apparently they have sealed off that passage. The monks heard some explosions and saw the zombies moving something off the ship.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.text: It seems they found the passage as they did a little interior rearranging.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.player: Well then, it looks like I'll go in through the front door.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.text: Hah, only if you can walk through wood! They sealed it with planks.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.player: Wait a moment... That ship has cannons, right?
Then I'll storm on board, grab some gunpowder and blow those doors off their hinges!
Oh, this is nothing. All in a day's work for me.
See you later, doctor. Whatever party they are planning in there, I have to go pick up my invitation.

talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
talking-to-dr-fenkenstrain-at-harmony-is.text: When you have all the equipment I asked for, come and see me so we can begin the procedure.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player searches the west chest on the main floor:

steps.text: If the player already has a fuse in their inventory:
You already have some fuse. You do not need any more.
If the player does not have inventory space:
You do not have enough free inventory space to take any fuse.
If the player has inventory space:
some fuse

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player takes the keg on the upper level:

steps.text: If the player already has a keg in their inventory:
You already have a barrel of gunpowder. You do not need another.
If the player does not have inventory space:
You do not have enough free inventory space to take that.
If the player has inventory space:
a keg

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player teleports away from the island with a fuse or keg in their inventory:

steps.text: For the sake of safety, you have to leave the [fuse/gunpowder] behind when you teleport.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player teleports away from the island with both the fuse and keg in their inventory:

steps.text: For the sake of safety, you have to leave the gunpowder behind when you teleport.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player is not directly in front of the temple door whilst using the fuse with the keg:

steps.text: I should put the keg where I want to detonate it before I attach the fuse.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player lights the fuse with a light source other than a tinderbox:

steps.text: Nothing interesting happens.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player lights the fuse with a tinderbox:

steps.text: You light the fuse...
The temple door explodes, leaving a sizeable hole.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player attempts to open the door after blowing it up:

steps.text: You can't open these doors any further without destroying the front of the building.
However, you can walking through the hole quite easily.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player attempts to peer-through the peephole from the temple side:

steps.text: You do not think there will be anything interesting to see through that.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player has a hammer:

steps.player: I have a hammer for you, doctor.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Very nice. Although, a sterilised one would be better.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player has several or all skull staples:

steps.player: I have some skull staples for you, doctor.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Hmmm, size 3 staples. Interesting...

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player has the cranial clamp:

steps.player: I have a cranial clamp for you, doctor.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Excellent, this will come in handy.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player has the brain tongs:

steps.player: I have a cranial clamp for you, doctor.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Wonderful...and they even have easy-grip handles, too.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player has only one bell jar:

steps.player: I have a bell jar for you, doctor.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: It's exactly this style of jar that I need, thank you.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player has more than one bell jar (or all three bell jars):

steps.player: I have some bell jars for you, doctor.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: It's exactly this style of jar that I need, thank you.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player does not have the required items:

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: When you have all the equipment I asked for, come and see me so we can begin the procedure.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: If the player hands in all the required items:

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Well, that's all of the items I'll need to get this situation fixed up.

steps.player: So we can begin immediately?

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: That's right.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Could you please keep notes of what I do, for posterity?

steps.player: Certainly. That and I'll be keeping an eye on you to make sure nothing 'untoward' happens to those brains.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Well, that is your prerogative.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Let us get this operation started. I'll begin by using the...
A redacted cutscene of Dr Fenkenstrain operating on a brain has been replaced with a kitten playing with a ball of string.
The previous scene was replaced with a picture of a kitten and some soothing music. We now return you to the adventure in progress.

steps.player: I don't want my eyes anymore!

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Pah, you have no stomach for science.

steps.player: I think I'm going to be sick...

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Well, if you are, do it in a bucket. This is a sterile environment, after all.

steps.player: But, but, it fell on the floor!

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Only a little, and the sawdust scraped right off with that cheese grater.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: Now, why not follow them upstairs while I clean up.

steps.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
steps.text: I'm sure as soon as their headaches fade, they will want to talk to you.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: I have been talking with some of the monks. They do seem to be rather intelligent for members of the clergy.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.text: The ones with brains, that is.

retrieving-the-items-for-dr-fenkenstrain.player: I'm sure that glowing review will endear you to them.

giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.player: I guessed. Look, I'm going to head out and kill this Mi- Gor joker before he can get his crew together and sail away.

giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.speaker: Brother Tranquility
giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.text: W-wait...I have a bad feeling about this...

giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.speaker: Brother Tranquility
giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.text: The pirates m-must have moved something large into the s-secret room to b-block it, and Mi-Gor mentioned he had a bodyguard.

giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.speaker: Brother Tranquility
giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.text: You should be prepared for a f-fierce battle.

giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.speaker: Brother Tranquility
giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.text: Have a word with the others. They will bless you before you leave.

giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.speaker: Brother Tranquility
giving-brother-tranquility-the-good-news.text: D-do you want me to take you back to the island?

talking-to-the-cured-monks-with-partial-.speaker: Monk
talking-to-the-cured-monks-with-partial-.text: Would you like to receive a blessing?
The monk blesses the player with a symbol of Saradomin over the player's head.
You feel the power of Saradomin restore your body.
The player is restored with full Prayer points.

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Well...ow...at least...oof...I'm back in the right body...

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: So...woozy...

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: Ow, ow...those staples sting a little...

steps.speaker: Monk
steps.text: This is the worst hangover ever...and I didn't even get drunk!

talking-to-the-cured-monks-with-full-pra.player: I think I'll come back when you feel a little better.

confronting-mi-gor.speaker: Mi-Gor
confronting-mi-gor.text: Wheeze!* You! I will peel you like a grape for your interference!

confronting-mi-gor.player: That's pretty big talk for someone who can't even breathe properly!}}

confronting-mi-gor.speaker: Mi-Gor
confronting-mi-gor.text: Wheeze!* Filthy little insect! Wretched little vermin! Let us see how witty you feel after my barrel-chested bodyguard has beaten you to paste!

confronting-mi-gor.player: Hah, I don't care how muscular your bodyguard is. I'll still defeat them!

confronting-mi-gor.text: Barrelchest rises up from the ground behind Mi-Gor.

confronting-mi-gor.speaker: Mi-Gor
confronting-mi-gor.text: Wheeze!* Hekhekhekhek... 'That' is my bodyguard, the Barrelchest!

confronting-mi-gor.speaker: Mi-Gor
confronting-mi-gor.text: Wheeze!* I was going to test his capabilities by letting him wipe out the monks, but I believe a little warm up is in order first.

confronting-mi-gor.speaker: Mi-Gor
confronting-mi-gor.text: Wheeze* And now I will take my leave.
Mi-Gor teleports away and Barrelchest strikes the player with its anchor.
If the player manages to kill Barrelchest:

steps.text: The Barrelchest has dropped its anchor! If you could get it fixed, then it would make a formidable weapon...

talking-to-brother-tranquility.player: Well, you'll not have to worry about Mi-Gor any more. I defeated his creation and he seems to have slipped away.

talking-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility.text: Yes, one of the brothers observed him and a few of his sorebones slipping into the water shortly after there was a loud bang from inside the building.

talking-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility.text: It is a pity he escaped, but Saradomin's justice will find him in the end.

talking-to-brother-tranquility.player: One thing does strike me as odd. He mentioned the name Rabid Jack, which I have heard in connection to zombie pirates before.
Can you tell me who that is?

talking-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility.text: I cannot, but I do recall hearing it before.

talking-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility.text: One of the pirates on the island said it while in the grip of a terrible fever. The others quietened him down and refused to answer any questions about it.

talking-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility.text: I have no doubt that they know who it is, but I get the feeling that they will not tell you.

talking-to-brother-tranquility.player: Hmm...I'm sure I might be able to get them to say if I persuade them.
Still, that's a job for another time. After all that work, I think I might take a bit of a rest.

talking-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility.text: Certainly! Saradomin blesses you for your valiant effort!

talking-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility.text: Here is a lamp blessed by Saradomin. If you pray over it, it will grant you wisdom.

talking-to-brother-tranquility.speaker: Brother Tranquility
talking-to-brother-tranquility.text: Oh, that? Sounds a little like locusts.

talking-to-brother-tranquility.player: Er, time for me to be off, I think.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-brother-t.speaker: Brother Tranquility
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-brother-t.text: A lot better, thanks. Can I help you with anything?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-brother-t.player: Not really. I was just popping by to see how you were all getting on and possibly help cull some of the zombies.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-brother-t.speaker: Brother Tranquility
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-brother-t.text: Your concern is most gratifying. Saradomin be with you.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-brother-t.speaker: Brother Tranquility
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-brother-t.text: Do you want me to take you back to Mos Le'Harmless?

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dr-fenken.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dr-fenken.text: After talking with these monks and seeing your efforts to save them...I'm starting to regret my past actions.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dr-fenken.player: Admittedly, most of us don't accidentally trip and sew a bunch of dead bodies together.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dr-fenken.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dr-fenken.text: I know...I think that my time here will be well spent trying to atone for what I did.

post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dr-fenken.speaker: Dr Fenkenstrain
post-quest-dialogue-talking-to-dr-fenken.text: Thank you for helping me see the error of my ways, [player name].
